answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. Only when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task, slashing occurs. This approach ensures a whisper of distrust among attackers, rendering their coordinated efforts futile. Like a relic of the past, Sybil attacks are left to gather dust, unable to reach the zenith of success.
